A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same AffordDexGrasp work, with matching core methods and main results. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally includes Supplemental Sections A-E. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support comparison.

before.justification: Tables 1-5 report original simulation comparisons, ablations, zero-shot and one-shot evaluations, and real-world grasping outcomes.

after.justification: Retains the original empirical results and adds diffusion comparisons, inference timings, affordance prediction measurements and a manipulation demonstration.

M1.justification: The core affordance representation, AFM, GFM and grasp optimization remain unchanged. Supplemental D.4 adds a manipulation procedure combining grasp generation with ReKep-style keypoint constraints, MLLM planning and an optimization solver. Other architectural elaborations document existing components.

E1.justification: The open-set, closed-set, zero-shot and one-shot grasping evaluations are retained. D.4 and Figure 14 add a real-world manipulation task involving pouring. The newly supplied category lists and one-shot dataset counts primarily document coverage already described in v1.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds DDIM and DDPM comparisons against flow matching. The original comparator sets remain. Contact2Gen becoming ContactGen and GraspCAVE becoming GraspCVAE are naming corrections, verified against their references, rather than new baselines.

E3.justification: The additional experiments introduce train/test Point IoU and component inference-time evaluation. Appendix B.1 reports 11 unseen categories for Open Set A, versus 10 in v1, constituting a reported setting correction without establishing a rerun. The 80/20 split and detailed retained evaluation procedures are newly disclosed information.

E4.justification: Supplemental D substantially expands the analyses: flow matching versus diffusion and computational cost, direct train/test affordance generalization, optimization before-and-after examples, and a downstream manipulation case study. These address questions beyond the retained representation, pre-understanding and optimization ablations in Table 2.

E5.justification: Table 7 newly reports timing values with ± quantities. Their statistical meaning and repetition counts are unspecified, so additional training runs or a particular uncertainty estimator cannot be inferred. Existing grasp-diversity standard deviations remain unchanged and measure output diversity.

E6.justification: Tables 1-5 retain their numerical results, and Table 6 reuses the unoptimized flow-matching results from Table 2. Substantial additions concern diffusion comparisons, inference cost and intermediate-map generalization: Table 8 reports test IoU of 0.508/0.502 versus contact-map 0.359/0.315 on A/B. Figure 14 adds a qualitative manipulation outcome.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly formalizes the evaluation encoder's multi-positive InfoNCE objective and category/action matching predicate in Equation 18. Appendix A.3 supplies explicit definitions for previously described optimization losses. Core Equations 1-7 are retained; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: open-set language-guided dexterous grasping, generalizable-instructive affordance, the two flow-matching models and superior open-set generalization. Supplementary evidence and application examples do not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: D.1 newly interprets flow matching as offering better performance and faster inference than diffusion, with modest affordance-generation overhead. D.4 discusses applicability to planned manipulation. Existing affordance and optimization interpretations remain; no substantive limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: Sections A-C and E substantially improve documentation through attention wiring, loss definitions, the previously referenced MLLM prompt, texture-generation prompts, category lists, camera placement, evaluation sampling and thresholds, baseline adaptations and robot execution details. These disclosures mostly clarify existing experiments rather than establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: Adds citations including DDPM, DDIM, Perceiver, InfoNCE, G-DexGrasp, AffordPose and newer interaction work. ReKep, already cited in v1, gains an explicit role in the manipulation extension. The related-work organization and principal novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are retained, with localized wording corrections, corrected method names, a rewritten split description, expanded author information and acknowledgements. Detailed explanations are appended in separately organized Supplemental Sections A-E rather than extensively rewriting the main paper.

P2.justification: Figures 5-15 and Tables 6-8 substantially expand the visual presentation with training and evaluation diagrams, prompt examples, dataset construction, comparative visualizations, hardware photographs and execution sequences. The original figures and tables largely retain their organization.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves important reproducibility gaps by supplying the previously referenced prompts and documenting evaluation sampling, success criteria, data construction and baseline adaptations. Added model-choice and affordance-generalization analyses strengthen validation while preserving the main results. Timing uncertainty remains undefined, and D.1's broad superiority interpretation exceeds the mixed grasp-quality evidence in Table 6, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial improvement in verifiability.
